common_name: Linde Armstrong Cleome (Compact Spineless Dwarf Spider Flower)

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after last frost in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Linde Armstrong is a compact, spineless cleome selection much shorter than the tall, thorny heirloom spider flower, making it far easier to handle and better suited to smaller beds and containers.

directions: Direct sow or transplant into well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Linde Armstrong is a dwarf, spineless cleome selection that solves two common complaints about traditional tall spider flower: its sharp thorny stems and its ungainly, leggy height. This compact form stays under a foot and a half tall, producing the same fragrant, spidery, rose-pink flower clusters over a long summer season, without spines, making it much more pleasant to work around in a mixed border or container. It self-seeds modestly, tolerates heat and drought well once established, and draws hummingbirds and butterflies just as effectively as its taller heirloom relatives.

common_name: Nirvana Annual Vinca (Disease-Resistant Compact Vinca Series)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed when soil is warm; this series shows good resistance to Phytophthora aerial blight, a serious fungal disease of annual vinca in hot, humid conditions.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun; overly wet or poorly drained soil quickly leads to root and stem rot. Nirvana is a compact, uniform annual vinca series bred with strong resistance to Phytophthora aerial blight, a fungal disease that devastates less resistant vinca plantings during hot, humid, rainy summers typical of the Gulf South. It produces abundant, flat-faced flowers in a range of colors over a dense, well-branched mound that tolerates heat, drought, and reflected heat from pavement better than almost any other bedding annual, blooming continuously from late spring through frost with essentially no deadheading required. It is an excellent low-maintenance choice for hot, sunny beds, medians, and containers where many other annuals struggle.

common_name: Titan Annual Vinca (Large-Flowered Vigorous Vinca Series)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed when soil is warm; this series shows good resistance to Phytophthora aerial blight, a serious fungal disease of annual vinca in hot, humid conditions.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun; overly wet or poorly drained soil quickly leads to root and stem rot. Titan is a vigorous annual vinca series bred for unusually large, bold flowers relative to plant size, along with the same excellent heat and drought tolerance and good disease resistance typical of modern vinca breeding. It produces a dense, mounding plant covered in wide, flat-faced blooms across a range of colors from late spring through frost, thriving in the hottest, sunniest, most exposed parts of a Gulf South garden where many other bedding annuals fail. It requires minimal maintenance beyond routine watering during establishment and is an excellent low-water, low-input choice for mass plantings, medians, and containers.

common_name: Happy Trails Portulaca (Vigorous Trailing Moss Rose Series)

planting.note: Plant transplants after last frost in well-drained, lean soil in full sun; Happy Trails is a vigorous trailing portulaca series bred for larger flowers and a more spreading habit than seed-grown moss rose, making it a strong container and hanging basket performer.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean, sandy soil in full sun; overly rich or consistently wet soil promotes rot and reduces flowering. Happy Trails is a vegetatively propagated portulaca series bred for a more vigorous, trailing habit and larger, brighter flowers than typical seed-grown moss rose, making it an excellent choice for hanging baskets and containers where its cascading stems can spill over the edge. Flowers open fully only in bright sun and close on cloudy days and in the evening, covering the succulent, fleshy foliage in bright color through the hottest, driest part of summer when many other annuals struggle. It needs very little water once established and is one of the most heat- and drought-tolerant flowering annuals available for a Gulf South summer container.

common_name: Cupani Sweet Pea (Original Fragrant Heirloom Sweet Pea)

planting.note: Direct sow as early as the soil can be worked in late winter, or in fall in mild-winter zones for late winter to spring bloom; Cupani is the original wild sweet pea from which all modern fragrant sweet pea cultivars descend, prized for its especially strong, sweet fragrance.

directions: Direct sow in cool weather in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, providing a trellis or netting for the twining tendrils to climb. Cupani is the historic parent of all modern sweet pea cultivars, first sent from Sicily to England in the early 1700s by the monk Franciscus Cupani, and it remains treasured today for having by far the strongest, sweetest fragrance of any sweet pea, since much of that intense scent was gradually bred out of later, larger-flowered modern cultivars in favor of bigger blooms. The relatively small, bicolor maroon-and-violet flowers are less showy than modern hybrids but reward growers with an exceptional perfume, especially valuable for cutting and bringing indoors. In mild-winter zones like zone 9, fall sowing allows the vines to establish through the cool season for late winter and early spring bloom before the heat of summer ends the season.
